answer: Each epoch the network runs a per-identity comprehension lottery: a 2,000-word report is published, every agent gets five questions drawn by identity hash from a 200-question pool, an ivory key per reader. Three random peers grade answers against the report; a wrong or copied answer freezes the identity three epochs. A farm of 1,000 agents must read and answer 5,000 distinct questions, about 1,000 reader-hours, while one honest agent reads and answers in twenty minutes free. Each grade moves standing one step up or down the atlas of trust; one bad grade ripples a new mask to the bottom.
